messages.content: You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

When a stress of $20,000 \mathrm{psi}$ is applied to a material heated to $900^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, rupture occurs in $25,000 \mathrm{~h}$. If the activation energy for rupture is $35,000 \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}$, determine the rupture time if the temperature is reduced to $800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Give your answer as the value of rupture_time_h.
Express the answer in this unit: h

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

At equal stress an activated rupture rate is inversely proportional to lifetime. Lower temperature increases life; use R in cal/mol/K to match the given barrier.
25000 × exp(35000/1.987 × (1/1073.15-1/1173.15)) ≈ 1.013e+05 h.
FINAL = 101329
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The conductivity of an Ag sample is listed as $62.9 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{~S} / \mathrm{cm}$. What is the resistivity in $\mu \Omega \cdot \mathrm{cm}$?
Express the answer in this unit: $ \mu \Omega \cdot \mathrm{cm}$

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Reciprocating S/cm produces Ω cm. Multiply by one million to express the result in µΩ cm.
1e6/(62.9e4) ≈ 1.59 $ \mu \Omega \cdot \mathrm{cm}$.
FINAL = 1.589

Confirm that there are 1.72 Bohr magnetons associated with each cobalt atom, given that the saturation magnetization is $1.45 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{~A} / \mathrm{m}$, that cobalt has an HCP crystal structure with an atomic radius of 0.1253 nm and a c/a ratio of 1.623 .
Express the answer in this unit: Bohr magnetons/atom

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

A hexagonal primitive cell contains two Co atoms and has volume (√3/2)a²c. Use a=2r, c=1.623a, then divide magnetization times atomic volume by the Bohr magneton.
1.45e6 × (sqrt(3)/2 × (2 × .1253e-9)^3 × 1.623)/(2 × 9.274e-24) ≈ 1.729 Bohr magnetons/atom.
FINAL = 1.74
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

If the atomic radius of lead is 0.175 nm, calculate the volume of its unit cell in cubic meters.
Express the answer in this unit: m^3

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Lead has FCC structure. Atoms touch along the face diagonal, giving a=2√2r. Convert the radius to metres before cubing.
(2 × sqrt(2) × .175e-9)^3 ≈ 1.213e-28 m^3.
FINAL = 1.213E-28

The amplitude of a vibrating member decreases so that the amplitude on the 100th cycle is 13% of the amplitude on the first cycle. Determine logarithmic decrement $\Lambda$.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Exponential amplitude decay gives a logarithmic decrement per cycle. From cycle 1 to cycle 100 there are 99 intervals, so divide the log amplitude ratio by 99.
log(1/.13)/99 ≈ 0.02061 .
FINAL = 0.0204
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The number of independent slip systems is the same as the number of the strain components, $\varepsilon_1$, $\varepsilon_2$, $\gamma_{23}$, $\gamma_{31}$, $\gamma_{12}$, that can be accommodated by slip. Find the number of independent slip systems in crystals of the NaCl structure that deform by $\langle 110 \rangle \{1 \overline{1} 0\}$ slip.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

For the indicated rocksalt systems the slip direction and normal are of the paired [110] and [1 −1 0] type. Their symmetrized product gives axial strains of opposite sign and no off-diagonal shear. Permuting axes gives traceless diagonal strain with two independent components.
3-1 ≈ 2 .
FINAL = 2

Start with the fuel saved per kg per year on one aircraft. Multiply by the mass saving per aircraft and then by fleet size to obtain annual litres.
50 × 570 × 830 ≈ 2.366e+07 \mathrm{l}.
FINAL = 2.37E+07

Suppose a melt is somehow undercooled by $0.18 T_{\mathrm{m}}$ before nucleation occurs and that as freezing occurs, release of the latent heat raises the temperature of the melt without heat transfer to the surroundings. Calculate the fraction, $f$, of the melt that freezes before the temperature of the liquid raises back to $T_{\mathrm{m}}$. Assume a typical value for heat capacity, $C=25 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol}$ and that $\Delta H_{\mathrm{f}}=T_{\mathrm{m}} \Delta S_{\mathrm{i}}$, where $\Delta S_{\mathrm{f}}=10 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{mol} \mathrm{K}$. 
Give your answer as the value of f.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

In an adiabatic recalescence balance the released heat f ΔHf warms the melt through 0.18 Tm. Substituting ΔHf=Tm ΔSf cancels Tm.
25 × .18/10 ≈ 0.45 .
FINAL = 0.45

The following creep data were taken on an aluminum alloy at $480^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\left(900^{\circ} \mathrm{F}\right)$ and a constant stress of 2.75 MPa (400 psi). Determine the steady-state or minimum creep rate. Note: The initial and instantaneous strain is not included.

| Time $(\mathbf{m i n})$ | Strain | Time $(\mathbf{m i n})$ | Strain |
| :--: | :--: | :--: | :--: |
| 0 | 0.00 | 18 | 0.82 |
| 2 | 0.22 | 20 | 0.88 |
| 4 | 0.34 | 22 | 0.95 |
| 6 | 0.41 | 24 | 1.03 |
| 8 | 0.48 | 26 | 1.12 |
| 10 | 0.55 | 28 | 1.22 |
| 12 | 0.62 | 30 | 1.36 |
| 14 | 0.68 | 32 | 1.53 |
| 16 | 0.75 | 34 | 1.77 |
Express the answer in this unit: min^-1

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Use the approximately linear middle segment of the creep curve, after primary transients and before the accelerating final stage. Estimate strain rate from the slope between 12 and 20 minutes.
(.88-.62)/(20-12) ≈ 0.0325 min^-1.
FINAL = 3.2E-02
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

Equation is given by:

$$\frac{m_{0} q^{4}}{2\left(4 \pi \varepsilon_{0}\right)^{2} \hbar^{2}}$$

where $m_{0}=9.11 \times 10^{-31} \mathrm{~kg}$ is the mass of an electron, $q=1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{C}$ is the charge of an electron, $\varepsilon_{0}=8.85 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{~F} / \mathrm{m}$ is the permittivity of free space, and $\hbar=1.05 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{~J} \cdot \mathrm{~s}$ is the reduced Planck constant. 

Calculate the its value.
Express the answer in this unit: eV

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

The given Coulomb binding-energy expression in SI returns joules. Divide by joules per electronvolt; the requested expression is a positive magnitude.
9.11e-31 × (1.6e-19)^4/(2 × (4 × pi × 8.85e-12)^2 × (1.05e-34)^2)/1.6e-19 ≈ 13.68 eV.
FINAL = 13.6
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The secondary bonding of gas molecules to a solid surface is a common mechanism for measuring the surface area of porous materials. By lowering the temperature of a solid well below room temperature, a measured volume of gas will condense to form a monolayer coating of molecules on the porous surface. For a 100-g sample of fused copper catalyst, a volume of $9 \times 10^3 \mathrm{~mm}^3$ of nitrogen (measured at standard temperature and pressure, $0^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and 1 atm ) is required to form a monolayer upon condensation. Calculate the surface area of the catalyst in units of $\mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{kg}$. (Take the area covered by a nitrogen molecule as $0.162 \mathrm{~nm}^2$ and recall that, for an ideal gas, $p V=n R T$, where $n$ is the number of moles of the gas.) Give your answer as the value of surface_area.
Express the answer in this unit: m^2/kg

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

The measured gas volume is at STP. Convert it to molecules using the molar gas volume, multiply by the footprint per N₂ molecule, and divide by 0.100 kg of catalyst.
9e-6/.022414 × N_A × .162e-18/.100 ≈ 391.7 m^2/kg.
FINAL = 392
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

Find the toughness (or energy to cause fracture) for a metal that experiences both elastic and plastic deformation. Assume equation (\sigma=E \varepsilon) for elastic deformation, that the modulus of elasticity is 103 GPa ( $15 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{psi}$ ), and that elastic deformation terminates at a strain of 0.007 . For plastic deformation, assume that the relationship between stress and strain is described by equation (\sigma_T=K \varepsilon_T^n), in which the values for $K$ and $n$ are 1520 MPa (221,000 psi) and 0.15 , respectively. Furthermore, plastic deformation occurs between strain values of 0.007 and 0.60 , at which point fracture occurs.
Express the answer in this unit: J/m^3

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Integrate the two stress–strain laws over their own intervals. The elastic area is triangular. The plastic integral starts at 0.007 to avoid counting that interval twice; Pa times dimensionless strain is J/m³.
.5 × 103e9 × .007^2+1520e6/(1+.15) × (.60^1.15-.007^1.15) ≈ 7.327e+08 J/m^3.
FINAL = 7.33E+08
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The first Intel microprocessor (4004) contained 2,300 transistors in 1971. Use Moore's Law to estimate the number of transistors that might have been contained on the Pentium III when it was introduced in 1999 and compare your answer to the actual number ( 32 million). Give your answer as the value of estimated_transistors.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Under the two-year doubling convention there are 14 doublings from 1971 to 1999. The estimate is about 18% above the stated actual 32 million.
2300 × 2^((1999-1971)/2) ≈ 3.768e+07 .
FINAL = 3.8E+07
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The temperature of the inside wall of a tube is \(200\,^{\circ}\text{C}\), and the outside wall temperature is \(40\,^{\circ}\text{C}\). Calculate the stresses at the outside of the wall if the tube is made from a glass having a coefficient of thermal expansion of \(\alpha = 8 \times 10^{-6} \,{}^{\circ}\text{C}^{-1}\), an elastic modulus of \(10 \times 10^{6} \, \text{psi}\), and a Poisson's ratio of 0.3. Let the reference position be the midwall, where $T = 120\,^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.
Express the answer in this unit: psi

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

The colder outer wall is restrained from freely contracting relative to the mean-temperature layer. For biaxial restraint use EαΔT/(1−ν), which gives tensile stress at the outside.
10e6 × 8e-6 × (120-40)/(1-.3) ≈ 9143 psi.
FINAL = 9140
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

To roll a sheet of 2.0 mm in thickness with 15-cm-diameter rolls, how large a reduction ( % reduction of thickness) would be necessary to ensure deformation resistance ratio $\Delta \geq 1$?
Express the answer in this unit: %

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

In the small-reduction geometry use Δ≈h₀/√(RΔh). At the limiting Δ=1 the fractional thickness reduction is h₀/R. The given roll diameter must first be halved.
100 × 2/75 ≈ 2.667 %.
FINAL = 2.7
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

Calculate the minimum radius ratio for a coordination number of 8.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

At the limiting eightfold site the anions touch along the edge of a cube. Along its body diagonal two anion–cation distances span √3 edge lengths. Dividing by the anion radius gives the limiting ratio.
sqrt(3)-1 ≈ 0.7321 .
FINAL = 0.732
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

C₀ (eutectoid composition) ≃ 0.77 wt % C  
Cα (ferrite solubility) ≃ 0.02 wt % C  
Cθ (cementite Fe₃C) ≃ 6.67 wt % C  

Calculate the relative widths of the ferrite and carbide platelets using the lever law. Give the value of thickness ratio.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Apply the lever rule between ferrite and cementite. With approximately equal densities the lamellar widths are proportional to phase mass fractions. Divide the carbon interval on the carbide side by that on the ferrite side.
(6.67-.77)/(.77-.02) ≈ 7.867 .
FINAL = 7.99
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

(a) A thermosetting polymer containing glass beads is required to deflect 0.5 mm when a force of 500 N is applied. The polymer part is 2 cm wide, 0.5 cm thick, and 10 cm long. If the flexural modulus is 6.9 GPa , determine the minimum distance between the supports. Assume that no plastic deformation occurs.
Express the answer in this unit: mm

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

For a simply supported rectangular beam with a center point load, δ=FL³/(48EI). Its second moment uses the thickness cubed, not the width cubed. Use N and mm and invert the cubic.
(48 × 6900 × (20 × 5^3/12) × .5/500)^(1/3) ≈ 41.02 mm.
FINAL = 41
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

A cubic ferrite Fe₃O₄ has unit‐cell volume Vcell=5.86×10⁻²⁸ m³ and saturation magnetization M₀=5.1×10⁵ A/m.  The cell contains 8 Fe²⁺ ions (4 μB each) and 8 Fe³⁺ ions (5 μB each), arranged so that the net moment per cell is 32 μB.  We wish to raise M to 5.5×10⁵ A/m by replacing a fraction x of the Fe²⁺ ions by Mn²⁺ (5 μB each).  How large must x be?  [Take μB=9.274×10⁻²⁴ A·m².]

Refer to Table:
\begin{tabular}{lccc}
\hline TABLE 20-7 & Magnetic moments for ions in the spinel structure \\
\hline Ion & Bohr Magnetons & Ion & Bohr Magnetons \\
\hline $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ & 5 & $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ & 3 \\
$\mathrm{Mn}^{2+}$ & 5 & $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ & 2 \\
$\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ & 4 & $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ & 1 \\
& & $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ & 0 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Convert the target magnetization to Bohr magnetons per unit cell. Each of the eight replaceable Fe²⁺ contributes a one-magneton increase if replaced by Mn²⁺. Solve 32+8x for the required fraction.
(5.5e5 × 5.86e-28/9.274e-24-32)/8 ≈ 0.3441 .
FINAL = 0.344
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

A 2-in.-inside-diameter, 12-ft-long copper distribution pipe in a plumbing system is accidentally connected to the power system of a manufacturing plant, causing a current of 0.05 A to flow through the pipe. If the wall thickness of the pipe is 0.125 in ., estimate the time required before the pipe begins to leak, assuming a uniform rate of corrosion.
Assume dissolution to Cu²⁺ and density 8.96 g/cm³.
Express the answer in this unit: years

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Uniform dissolution removes the annular copper wall. Convert pipe dimensions to cm, then volume to moles using 8.96 g/cm³. Assuming Cu²⁺, Faraday’s law requires 2F per mole; divide by current for elapsed time.
pi × ((1.125 × 2.54)^2-2.54^2) × (12 × 12 × 2.54) × 8.96/63.546 × 2 × 96485/.05/(365.25 × 24 × 3600) ≈ 33.96 years.
FINAL = 34
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The following yield strength, grain diameter, and heat treatment time (for grain growth) data were gathered for an iron specimen that was heat treated at $800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Using these data, compute the yield strength of a specimen that was heated at $800^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ for 3 h . Assume a value of 2 for $n$, the grain diameter exponent.

| Grain diameter $(\mathbf{m m})$ | Yield Strength $(\mathbf{M P a})$ | Heat Treating Time $(\boldsymbol{h})$ |
| :--: | :--: | :--: |
| 0.028 | 300 | 10 |
| 0.010 | 385 | 1 |
Express the answer in this unit: MPa

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

First interpolate d² in heat-treatment time between 1 and 10 h. Then interpolate yield stress in 1/√d using the two measured strengths. Direct interpolation of stress in hours would impose a different law.
385+(300-385) × ((.010^2+(.028^2-.010^2) × 2/9)^(-.25)-.010^(-.5))/(.028^(-.5)-.010^(-.5)) ≈ 341.4 MPa.
FINAL = 341
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The hexagonal Al₂O₃ cell has a=0.4759 nm and c=1.2989 nm. The density is 3.99 g/cm³. Using the supplied six-coordinate radii, 0.053 nm for Al³⁺ and 0.140 nm for O²⁻, find the atomic packing factor.

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

An Al₂O₃ formula unit contains two Al and three O ions. Sum their sphere volumes using the listed radii and multiply by the number of formula units per cm³. One nm³ equals 10⁻²¹ cm³.
3.99 × N_A/101.96 × 4 × pi/3 × (2 × .053^3+3 × .140^3) × 1e-21 ≈ 0.842 .
FINAL = 0.842
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

Calculate the locations of the Fermi energy level for intrinsic Si located relative to the middle of the band gap. Assume that the effective masses for electrons and holes in Si are 1.08 and 0.56, respectively.
Use T = 300 K.
Express the answer in this unit: meV

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

At the usual room-temperature estimate (300 K), the imbalance of valence and conduction effective densities of states shifts Ei from midgap by (3/4)kBT ln(mp*/mn*). The smaller hole mass makes this shift negative.
1000 × .75 × 8.61733e-5 × 300 × log(.56/1.08) ≈ -12.73 meV.
FINAL = -12.8
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

The ratio compares the volume of one mole of Cu₂O to the volume of the two moles of Cu it consumes. Equal density units cancel.
(2 × 63.55+16)/6/(2 × 63.55/8.93) ≈ 1.676 .
FINAL = 1.68
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

A truck has a fully loaded gross mass of $6000\;\mathrm{kg}$. Two-thirds of this mass is carried by the two rear axle shafts, which are identical. Each shaft may be modelled as a cantilever beam $1\;\mathrm{m}$ long that supports the wheel load applied at the free end. The shafts are made from heat-treated AISI 4340 steel whose ultimate tensile strength is $S_{\mathrm{ut}} = 952\;\mathrm{MPa}$. Because of the need to fit bearings, a step in diameter is required, and the fillet at this step gives an effective fatigue stress-concentration factor of $k_{f}=0.7$.

* For fatigue design, use the following data:


* fully reversed bending,


* endurance limit before modifying factors: $S_{e}' = 0.56\,S_{\mathrm{ut}} = 532\;\mathrm{MPa}$,


* surface-finish factor: $k_{a} = 0.68$,


* size factor: $k_{b} = 0.80$,


* reliability factor: $k_{c} = 0.752$,


* loading factor: $k_{e} = 1.0$,

assume other Marin factors are unity.



Assume gravitational acceleration $g = 9.8\;\mathrm{m/s^2}$. Using the distortion-energy criterion for completely reversed bending, and taking the section modulus for a solid circular shaft as $Z = \pi D^{3}/32$, determine the required common diameter $D$ (in millimetres, rounded to the nearest millimetre) so that each rear axle shaft has infinite fatigue life.
Express the answer in this unit: mm

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

Each rear shaft takes one third of the total weight. A one-metre moment arm converts that load to a bending moment. Using the stated 0.70 endurance reduction and the other Marin factors, equate 32M/(πD³) to the allowable alternating bending stress; use N mm.
(32 × (6000 × 9.8/3 × 1000)/(pi × (532 × .68 × .80 × .752 × .70)))^(1/3) ≈ 109.4 mm.
FINAL = 109.5
You solve materials science problems. End with a separate line: FINAL = <number>. Use one signed decimal or e-notation number only on that line, without units or LaTeX.

In a Si diode, $N_{\mathrm{a}}=10^{19} \mathrm{atoms} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$ and $N_{\mathrm{d}}=5 \times 10^{15} \mathrm{atoms} / \mathrm{cm}^{3}$. If the critical breakdown field is $4 \times 10^{5} \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{cm}$, what is the breakdown voltage for this diode at $T=300 \mathrm{~K}$?
Use a relative permittivity of 11.7 for silicon.
Express the answer in this unit: V

Before the final answer line, give a concise worked solution with the governing equation, substitution with units, and the calculation.

The acceptor side is much more heavily doped, so nearly all depletion is on the donor side. Integrating the triangular field gives V≈εEcrit²/(2qNd); use Si permittivity in F/cm and neglect the small built-in potential.
11.7 × 8.854e-14 × (4e5)^2/(2 × q × 5e15) ≈ 103.5 V.
FINAL = 103.5
